en: Udāna 7.8 Kaccānasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now on that occasion the Venerable Mahākaccāna was sitting not far from the Blessed One, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him by means of mindfulness directed to the body, well-established within and facing inward.

The Blessed One saw the Venerable Mahākaccāna sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness directed to the body, well-established within and facing inward.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For one who would always have mindfulness,
constantly established with the body as its object;”
"May it not be for me, nor may it come to be for me;
it will not be, nor will it come to be for me"—
dwelling there in successive stages, he...
Cross over the attachment by means of time itself.
